title: KV cache: tenant surge absorption & TTL stabilization playbook
creator: Priya Desai
description: This ticket captures the follow-up work and playbook for a multi-tenant KV cache incident where a rapid tenant traffic surge combined with TTL desynchronization and a compaction stall caused memory amplification and elevated latency. The goal is to document mitigations that reduce blast radius during tenant surges, stabilize TTL behavior across replicas, and prevent future compaction/eviction cascades.
background: On 2025-02-12 a subset of Dedicated nodes experienced sustained memory growth and elevated 99th-percentile latency. Root cause analysis showed a tenant produced many short-lived keys with inconsistent TTLs, causing the prefix index to grow and prefetched entries to accumulate. Concurrently a recently-merged async compaction optimization introduced a path where compaction could be delayed when the eviction queue was saturated, allowing memory to spike and eviction heuristics to oscillate.
timeline:
2025-02-12 09:14 UTC - First alerts triggered (high mem, latency).
2025-02-12 09:22 UTC - Routing fallback enabled for affected pool; partial traffic shifted.
2025-02-12 09:40 UTC - Hotfix applied: temporarily disabled aggressive prefetch and enabled per-tenant soft-cap enforcement.
2025-02-12 11:10 UTC - Memory growth stabilized; full traffic restored after verification.
2025-02-13 through 2025-02-18 - RCA investigation and instrument integration.
impact: Duration ~2 hours of degraded response times for customers on the affected Dedicated pool with increased error rates for large-batch generation jobs. Some customers saw API timeouts and automatic fallbacks to cheaper models. No data loss; all keys remained logically intact. Financial exposure due to SLA credits and support load was material for a handful of enterprise customers.
root_cause:
1) Workload pattern: a tenant generated a high volume of ephemeral keys with heterogeneous TTLs which prevented efficient prefix eviction and produced large transient prefix trees.
2) Eviction hysteresis: eviction score decay parameters were tuned too aggressively for steady-state but too sensitive during bursts, causing oscillation.
3) Compaction backpressure: async compaction could be starved when eviction queue depth was high, delaying reclaim and amplifying memory growth.
4) Missing guardrails: lack of per-tenant soft memory caps and insufficient telemetry on TTL distribution meant the system couldn't automatically throttle the offending tenant sooner.
short_term_actions:
- Ship a hotfix that enforces per-tenant soft caps (memory token bucket) and drops prefetch for tenants that exceed burst thresholds.
- Revert/patch the compaction scheduling change to include minimum reservation for compaction work during eviction storms.
- Add an automated runbook action that shifts traffic from affected pool to secondary pool after X minutes of sustained mem growth.
- Notify impacted customers and schedule targeted post-incident review with account teams.
long_term_actions:
- Implement TTL normalization: canonicalize TTLs at write time for short lived entries (bucketed TTLs) to improve eviction locality.
- Introduce eviction hysteresis tuning per-tenant with ramp-up/ramp-down windows to prevent oscillation.
- Rework compaction scheduler to guarantee background compaction quantum even under heavy eviction pressure and add backpressure signals to the ingress layer.
- Add per-tenant prefetch limits and smarter prefetch heuristics that consider TTL distributions.
- Build synthetic chaos tests that simulate tenant surge patterns and validate soft-cap behavior in CI.
- Add billing/usage alerts tied to sudden burst patterns to trigger optional throttles or grace-period controls for customers.
tests:
- Unit and integration tests for per-tenant token bucket enforcement.
- Load test scenario (kvmem-surge-100k-ephemeral) to be added to perf harness; verify eviction recovery within 3 minutes and <10% request error rate.
- Canary release against 5% of Dedicated fleet with increased metrics retention and flamegraphs enabled.
- Regression test for compaction scheduler ensuring compaction quantum preserved when eviction queue > 80%.
monitoring:
- New metrics: tenant_memory_tokens_used, tenant_prefetch_skips, compaction_reserved_threads, ttl_distribution_90p_bucket.
- Alert: tenant_memory_tokens_used > 0.9 for 2m AND compaction_reserved_threads < 1 -> page SRE.
- Dashboards: per-tenant prefix-tree-size heatmap, eviction-score-variance, compaction-lag histogram.
- Add logging context: tenant_id, prefix_hash, sample_kv_keys for top offending prefixes when eviction rate spikes.
rollout_plan: 1) Ship hotfix to control plane and runtime (runtime-1.22.hotfix). 2) Canary on 3 Dedicated nodes for 24 hours with synthetic surge tests. 3) Gradual 10/25/50/100% rollout over 48 hours if canary metrics stable. 4) Post-rollout review and close ticket after 7 days of stable telemetry.
